dispositions.change: Root cause was G0A2-1 (consuming FakeRunner). With C1's semantics corrected, Task 15's whole gate is green and its count was re-derived from a real --through-15 materialisation: 32 passed (8 projections + 24 orchestrator), not the stated 21.

FakeRunner unified on ONE semantics and documented in its docstring: first match in insertion order; an entry is CONSUMED only when another entry with an IDENTICAL prefix follows it later in the list. A prefix recorded once is sticky; N recordings play in order with the last sticky. Both consumer sets are satisfied.

Every Step-2/Step-4 count re-derived by verify-steps.py, which materialises the plan THROUGH each task from its own labelled blocks and runs the exact command the task names. Tasks 11/14/15/19/21/22/23 restated (24, 24, 32, 16, 18 PASS rows, 4 passed, 13 passed + 60/60). dispositions.change: Dry-run rows are now stamped simulated:true with their PLANNED effects under planned_writes; plan_digest_line renders effective_writes(row) and tags simulated lines, so the digest built from a dry-run ledger reports its simulated changes instead of collapsing to zero.

A dry-run over a new-but-domain-matched sender now assigns the prospective id '<new:<email>>' after the upsert preview and still emits plan_add_interaction_argv, so the interaction row the live run will write is previewed. The preview header also emits the literal source_ref token.

The unchanged-recheck half is now pinned by ledger BYTES and row COUNT, not by the absence of a claude call; G-IDEMP-2's sed (`if False:`) makes it fail. The assertion moved out of the retired Task-8 file into the shipped one.
_send_escalation checks the runner rc and raises EscalationError; the message aborts with NO escalated row persisted, so escalated_for cannot gate the retry forever.

Failure receipts now carry this run's partial message_count + truncation (and model_receipt on the budget path), and _persist_partial writes a `partial` ledger row whenever an extraction exists — so a message that failed mid-write keeps its PAID extraction as the cache and the retry makes zero new claude calls.

normalize_owner folds the bus's own assignee identities ('human','user') onto 'josh'; a task this release created with --assignee human now dedups the identical commitment on the next run. Other agent assignees stay distinct.
The behaviour was always right; its only test was red because of the consuming FakeRunner. With C1 fixed the test is green, and G-CRM-2/G-HIST-2 now both record control_green + mutated_red.

Two halves. (a) Shape validation: ensure_contact accepts only a slugified id, write_interaction requires an interaction record carrying contact_id+source_ref FOR THIS contact, create_task requires task_<epoch>_<digits>. (b) Partial progress: a mid-message WriterError/EscalationError persists a `partial` row with the writes that DID land plus the already-filed resolutions; is_terminal refuses partial rows, and _merge_resolutions stops the retry re-writing them.
new_violations now keys a missing-ref violation on (ref, page), so the same ref later going missing from a DIFFERENT page is a new violation.

_superseded_task_ids was correct; its only exercising test was red. That test now renders real change lines (G-DIG-1 is repointed at it), so the full-history lookup and the list_open_tasks join are both green and mutation-proven.

gmail_section's change lines are asserted verbatim against plan_digest_line's output INCLUDING the extraction summary, on a row that now carries one; and the parity test compares the dry-run's digest-preview lines to the real gmail_section output.

Task 8's focused gate re-run against the real siblings from a --through-8 materialisation: 6 passed (the stated count is now true, where the round-2 run gave 1 failed/5 passed under the consuming FakeRunner).

The same-page test queues one response PER contact id (longer argv prefixes) and the shared FakeRunner's sticky semantics serve the rest. Task 8's incompatible file is retired by a `<!-- retire: -->` directive in Task 15 Step 5, so it is no longer collected by G1.

capture now emits base_sha (git rev-parse HEAD in the measured tree, fail-closed); check requires it, verifies it resolves, fails on any git diff error, and reconciles vitest_rc/pytest_rc against the parsed failing sets.
